title: Copilot Studio: express mode speeds up flows called by an agent or app
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, maker toggle, administrator controls, licensing and preview limits are supported. The summary should describe completing within two minutes as more likely, not guaranteed.

claims.quote: Select Flows, and then select the flow for which you want to turn on express mode.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2026-07-10T21:58:35.
The roadmap describes faster run times and fewer timeout failures as providing timely, reliable responses to agents and apps.
claims.quote: Express mode ensures agents and apps receive timely and reliable responses by dramatically accelerating flow run times. This reduces flow failures, improves user experience, and eliminates costly interruptions caused by timeout issues.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Turning on express mode helps called flows finish inside the two-minute window.
claims.quote: This feature increases the likelihood that agent flows can complete within the two-minute window and provide a response in time.
claims.fix: In the summary, replace 'so flows called by an agent or app finish inside the two-minute window' with 'to increase the likelihood that flows called by an agent or app finish inside the two-minute window'.

claims.claim: Express mode supports flows with the When an agent calls a flow trigger.
claims.quote: The flow must have either the When an agent calls a flow or the When an app calls a flow trigger.

claims.claim: Express mode supports flows with the When an app calls a flow trigger.
claims.quote: The flow must have either the When an agent calls a flow or the When an app calls a flow trigger.

claims.claim: Express mode requires a Response action, with Respond to agent an accepted action.
claims.quote: The flow must have a Response action, either Respond to agent or Respond to app.

claims.claim: Respond to app is an accepted Response action for express mode.
claims.quote: The flow must have a Response action, either Respond to agent or Respond to app.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The flow must have a Copilot Studio plan associated with it.
claims.quote: The flow must have a Copilot Studio plan associated with it.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope
claims.claim: Express mode is available only in upgraded Power Automate environments on the new infrastructure.
claims.quote: Express mode is currently only available only for upgraded environments using the new supported architecture.

claims.claim: An agent flow called by an agent or app fails if it takes longer than two minutes to respond, affecting the caller.
claims.quote: By default, an agent or app initiates an agent flow that fails if it takes longer than two minutes to respond to the calling agent or app. This failure affects the functionality and usability of the agent or app that calls the flow.

claims.claim: With express mode on, flows must still complete in two minutes or time out.
claims.quote: When you turn on express mode, flows must complete in two minutes. Flows that take longer time out.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn documents express mode as preview and prerelease documentation subject to change.
claims.quote: This article contains Microsoft Copilot Studio preview documentation and is subject to change.

claims.claim: The maker path is Copilot Studio: Flows > flow > Overview > Details > Edit > Express mode.
claims.quote: Select Flows, and then select the flow for which you want to turn on express mode. In the Details section of the Overview page, select Edit. The Details panel appears. Turn on Express mode.

claims.claim: Makers can also turn on express mode on the agent or app trigger card in the flow designer.
claims.quote: You can also turn on express mode from the When an agent calls a flow or the When an app calls a flow trigger itself while you're building the flow in the designer on the trigger card.

claims.where: controls[0].api; controls[0].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No API for the express mode toggle is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio agent flow express mode API workflow clientdata expressmode PowerShell; "express mode" "API". Opened express-mode documentation and Work with cloud flows using code; searched the latter for express and PATCH. No toggle property or operation found.

claims.where: controls[1]; summary; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant or environment administrator switch for express mode is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio express mode tenant environment administrator setting default enabled toggle. Opened agent-flow-express-mode, Tenant settings and Manage feature settings; searched the latter for express. No express-mode administrator setting found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature is user-opt-in: makers choose express mode per flow, with no documented administrator switch.
claims.quote: Select Flows, and then select the flow for which you want to turn on express mode. ... Turn on Express mode. The toggle is at the bottom of the panel.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the express mode toggle is off or on by default on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: "express mode" "default"; Copilot Studio express mode tenant environment administrator setting default enabled toggle. Read the roadmap and express-mode page. The page's 'By default' describes response timeouts, not the initial toggle state.

claims.claim: No source says existing flows change behaviour by themselves when express mode arrives.
claims.quote: Searched: "express mode" "existing flows" "automatically". Read roadmap record, agent-flow-express-mode and environment-architecture. Automatic environment upgrades are described, but automatic enabling of express mode on existing flows is not.

claims.claim: Microsoft is upgrading environments to support express mode.
claims.quote: Microsoft is in the process of upgrading environments to support express mode.

claims.claim: The express mode page says administrators do not need to act to upgrade their environment.
claims.quote: You don't need to take any action to upgrade your environment.

claims.claim: The new architecture required for express mode is SelfHost Multitenant.
claims.quote: To access faster runtimes and new features like express mode, your environment needs to be on SelfHost Multitenant architecture.

claims.claim: Some flows might block an environment upgrade, and Microsoft recommends updating those flows.
claims.quote: Some flows might block environment upgrades. We strongly recommend you update these flows, which unblock environment upgrades.

claims.claim: The architecture page documents checking the environmentFlowHostingType value.
claims.quote: Press Ctrl + Alt + A to view environment debug info and search for environmentFlowHostingType.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Checking for the toggle on a suitable trigger card tests availability; a missing toggle means the environment does not support express mode yet.
claims.quote: Check for the express mode toggle in the designer on the trigger card. If express mode doesn't appear, your environment doesn't support this feature yet.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Data-heavy flows can exceed express mode's memory limit and are unsuitable for it.
claims.quote: Large data amounts exceed the memory limit of express mode

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Change & support; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The message size limit for data passed in an individual action's connector response is 64 KB.
claims.quote: The message size limit for data passed in an individual action (connector response) is 64 KB.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Change & support; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Variable content is limited to 1,024 characters.
claims.quote: Variable content limit: 1,024 characters.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Delay actions are unsupported with express mode on.
claims.quote: Delay and webhook actions in the flow aren't supported when express mode is turned on.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Webhook actions are unsupported with express mode on.
claims.quote: Delay and webhook actions in the flow aren't supported when express mode is turned on.

claims.claim: Unsupported Delay or webhook actions produce errors when saving the flow.
claims.quote: Errors appear when saving the flow. For such cases, try turning off express mode and try again.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends no more than 100 actions per run as a safe limit, but more can work depending on flow size and processing.
claims.quote: 100 actions is a safe limit for flow size. In practice, you might be able to include more than 100 actions, depending on how large the flow is, and on how much data processing the flow does.

claims.claim: The actions count includes loops, counting one action for each loop iteration.
claims.quote: The actions count includes loops, which count as one action for each loop iteration.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An Apply to each loop is limited to 100 array items.
claims.quote: Apply to each loop on an array: max 100 items

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A Do until loop is limited to 100 iterations.
claims.quote: Do until loop: max 100 iterations

claims.claim: Automatic testing does not work in the flow designer for these flows.
claims.quote: Test your flow automatically doesn't work in the flow designer. Testing automatically uses flow resubmit, and flow resubmit can't be used with agent-triggered or app-triggered flows.

claims.claim: Loop iterations may be missing from Run details when a connector response exceeds the memory limit.
claims.quote: Loop iterations don't appear in the Run details view when a connector response exceeds the memory limit.

claims.claim: Live activity does not display during an express mode run.
claims.quote: In Express mode, live activity doesn't display while the flow is running.

claims.claim: Runtime error messages detail which documented runtime limitation caused a flow failure.
claims.quote: The runtime error messaging details why the flow failed if it's due to any of the previously mentioned runtime limitations.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises turning off express mode for a flow with a runtime data-limitation error.
claims.quote: If you encounter a flow runtime error mentioning a data limitation, turn off express mode, and try it with other flows instead.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends testing a flow in a development environment before publishing.
claims.quote: Test your flow in a development environment, and then turn on express mode for debugging before you publish to production.

claims.claim: Variable-size or memory-limit failures in tests indicate likely failures when deployed to production.
claims.quote: Express mode fails during test due to a variable size limit or memory limit. If the flow fails during a test, you're likely to hit these issues when the flow is deployed and run in production.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft's express mode page describes no new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: "express mode" "identity" "access" "connections"; Copilot Studio express mode data access connections identity default existing flows. Read agent-flow-express-mode in full. It describes execution performance and data-size limits, not new data access.

claims.claim: The express mode page does not describe changes to flow connections or execution identity.
claims.quote: Searched: "express mode" "identity" "access" "connections". Read agent-flow-express-mode and Create an agent flow as a tool. The express-mode page does not state a connection or execution-identity change.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Express mode entitlement is included with the Copilot Studio plan and is available only for flows under that plan.
claims.quote: Express mode is available only for flows under the Copilot Studio plan. There's no added cost to running your flows in this mode.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Running a flow in express mode adds no surcharge.
claims.quote: There's no added cost to running your flows in this mode.

claims.where: front matter: cost; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Actions remain billed under Copilot Studio metering, supporting a variable cost rating.
claims.quote: You're still billed for the number of actions used under Copilot Studio metering.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No separate express mode licence is documented; its prerequisites name a Copilot Studio plan.
claims.quote: Searched: "express mode" "no separate" "license"; Copilot Studio express mode price rate separate license budget cap. Read express-mode Prerequisites and Licensing and Billing rates and management. No separate express-mode licence found.

claims.claim: Express mode uses the existing agent-flow action meter, counted by actions.
claims.quote: Agent flow actions per 100 actions | 13 Copilot Credits

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Agent-flow test runs are exempt from capacity consumption for agent-flow actions.
claims.quote: Agent flow runs that the agent starts from the test chat in Copilot Studio and test runs that you start in the flow designer, don't consume capacity for agent flow actions and aren't blocked by enforcement.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Qualifying agent-triggered flow actions are included at no charge while an authenticated Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed user interacts with the agent.
claims.quote: When a user who is authenticated with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license interacts with an agent, and the agent calls an agent flow that uses the When an agent calls the flow trigger, the agent flow actions are included at no charge.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Autonomous-agent flow runs are not covered by that exemption.
claims.quote: Agent flow runs called by an autonomous agent consume Copilot Credits and are subject to enforcement, even if the users in your organization have Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses.

claims.claim: AI tools inside an agent flow are metered separately from agent-flow actions.
claims.quote: These exemptions apply to agent flow actions. AI tools that run inside an agent flow, such as prompts, are metered separately.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate express mode rate.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio express mode price rate separate license budget cap; "express mode" "cost" "admin". Read agent-flow-express-mode Licensing and Billing rates and management. Existing action metering is stated; no separate express-mode rate found.

claims.claim: No cap or budget control specific to express mode is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "express mode" "budget" "licence"; Copilot Studio express mode price rate separate license budget cap. Read express-mode documentation and Billing rates and management. General flow capacity enforcement is documented, but no express-mode-specific budget control.

claims.claim: The disable-flow path is Power Platform admin center: Manage > Environments > environment > Resources > Flows > flow > Disable.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Manage. ... select Environments. ... select an environment. In the Resources web part, select Flows. ... select the flow you want to manage. ... Disable or Enable | Disable or enable the flow.

claims.claim: Disable-AdminFlow -EnvironmentName <environment name> -FlowName <flow name> stops the targeted flow using Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell.
claims.quote: Module: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell Module. Stops the specified flow. Disable-AdminFlow -EnvironmentName <String> -FlowName <String> [-ApiVersion <String>] [<CommonParameters>]

claims.claim: Environment Admin, Global admin and Power Platform admin can manage and disable flows.
claims.quote: If you're an Environment Admin, Global admin, or Power Platform admin, you can manage the flows created in your organization. ... Disable the flow

claims.claim: Disabling a flow stops the whole flow rather than changing only its express mode setting.
claims.quote: The Disable-AdminFlow cmdlet stops the specified flow.

claims.claim: The existing administrator control can enable a flow as well as disable it.
claims.quote: Disable or Enable | Disable or enable the flow.

claims.claim: The express mode Learn page names no administrator role for its maker toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio express mode tenant environment administrator setting default enabled toggle. Read agent-flow-express-mode, including Prerequisites and Turn on express mode. No administrator role is named for the toggle.
